news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway projects £764k overspend on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools
news_drafts.lead:
Dumfries and Galloway Council's education service projects overspends on two budget lines for 2026/27: £764k on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools. The figures are in the second-quarter revenue budget monitoring report for the Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee, which meets on 10 November.

Supporting Learners has a projected out-turn of £22.705m against a revised budget of £21.941m. Additional support for learning (ASL) generic support is the largest single variance. It is projected at £1.143m over its revised budget of £13.149m. Education Psychologists, Sensory Services and Targeted Support are each projected under budget.

The primary schools line, which includes Learning Centres, has a projected out-turn of £60.288m against a revised budget of £60.035m. The paper records a £1.038m budget adjustment in 2026/27 before that revised budget was set.
news_drafts.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Appendix 1

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway: Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary allocation left a gap of about £10m
news_drafts.lead:
The money Dumfries and Galloway Council had agreed for Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary School does not cover the costs identified for the two schools, leaving a funding gap of around £10m. The figure is in an appendix to the council's capital investment programme, its planned spending on things that last, such as buildings, over the next few years.

The council's Education and Learning Committee agreed on 23 May 2024 that the existing allocation was not enough. That allocation is part of £73.975m in the programme. The appendix says: "Previously agreed capital allocation (part of the £73.975m) is not enough to cover the values identified, so Members also agreed to request the funding gap, circa £10m, from FTP committee."

FTP is the Finance, Procurement and Transformation Committee. The papers quoted here do not say how that committee responded to the request.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

findings.paper_title: C&D Hos 6 Month Performance Report - Appendix 1
findings.headline: Sickness absence for non-teacher local government employees in Customer and Digital is reported at 7.04 days per employee in H1 2026/27, against a target of 4.5 days and 5.59 days in H1 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper reports the average days lost per non-teacher employee through sickness absence (CW03_CD) and the percentage of possible attendances lost (CW04_CD). Both are above target and above the H1 2025/26 values. The annual target for both is shown as 4.5 days and 4% respectively.
findings.matters: Higher absence reduces available staff capacity and can add cover costs, and the same risk register lists high sickness absence as a risk to the service.
findings.quote: Percentage of days lost per employee through sickness absence as a percentage of total

findings.paper_title: C&D Hos 6 Month Performance Report - Appendix 1
findings.headline: Customer and Digital's risk of overspending on the ICT and Digital budget is recorded as having no issues identified to date, with monthly meetings with Finance continuing.
findings.detail: Risk CD03 concerns overspending on the ICT and Digital budget, including higher-than-forecast energy, fuel, broadband, telephony and rates costs. The October 2026 latest position states that regular monthly meetings with Finance continue, that no issues have been identified to date, and that the risk remains.
findings.matters: It shows how a service is tracking a specific overspend risk against inflation-exposed costs and says the risk is still open, which is relevant to finance directors monitoring ICT cost pressure.
findings.figures: Risk CD03 is reviewed in October 2026. No monetary figures for the ICT and Digital budget are given in the paper.
findings.quote: To date no issues have been identified however the risk still remains

findings.paper_title: C&D Hos 6 Month Performance Report - Appendix 1
findings.headline: Customer and Digital's projected revenue budget outturn is reported at 100% of budget for 2026/27, the same as 2025/26.
findings.detail: The service's finance indicator CW19_CD shows a projected outturn of 100% of budget for H1 2026/27, against a target of 100%. The H1 2025/26 value was also 100%. The paper reports no variance on this measure.
findings.matters: A service reporting its projected outturn exactly on budget, with no variance, is a point of comparison for finance officers tracking directorate-level forecasting.
findings.figures: CW19_CD projected outturn: 100% of budget (H1 2026/27); target 100%; H1 2025/26 value 100%.

findings.headline: Telephony contract renewal procurement is on target to conclude by end of November 2026
findings.detail: The corporate telephony system upgrade, carried over from 2025/26, is due to complete this year. Procurement colleagues are supporting the renewal of the associated telephony contracts. Capital has been provisionally set aside in case some associated hardware needs replacing, which will only be known during procurement.
findings.matters: A contract renewal that is on schedule, with a contingency held for hardware, is a point of comparison for other councils renewing core telephony and its capital contingencies.
findings.quote: which is on target to be concluded by end of November 2026.

findings.headline: Wireless infrastructure replacement expects in-year spend slippage, with the allocated budget still expected to be spent this financial year
findings.detail: The wireless infrastructure order is being finalised with legal and procurement colleagues, and equipment is expected in Q3 and Q4 onwards. This will cause some slippage in the in-year spend profile, but the council expects the allocated budget to be achieved this year. The overall FY2026/27 allocation of £1.419 Million includes £294k carried forward from FY2025/26.
findings.matters: The paper separates in-year spend timing from the full-year budget outcome, which shows how a capital scheme's cash profile can move while the allocation is still expected to be used.
findings.figures: £1.419 Million FY2026/27 allocation including £294k slippage carried forward from FY2025/26; £1.125 Million recurring allocation in subsequent years
findings.quote: As a result, some slippage within our in year spend profile is expected; but the allocated budget is still expected to be achieved this financial year.
